subject: HASS
description: HASS complete progression map — 31 year levels, 333 standards, 17 strands. Merged from 10 source files.

standards.title: Family structures and roles over time
standards.description: differences in family structures and roles today, and how these have changed or remained the same over time
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain differences in family structures and roles today, and how these have changed or remained the same over time.

standards.title: Daily life continuity and change
standards.description: continuity and change between aspects of their daily lives and their parents’ and grandparents’ childhoods
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify continuity and change between aspects of their daily lives and their parents’ and grandparents’ childhoods.

standards.title: Features of local places
standards.description: the natural, managed and constructed features of local places, and their location
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify the natural, managed and constructed features of local places, and their location.

standards.title: Changing and caring for places
standards.description: how places change and how they can be cared for by different groups including First Nations Australians
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how places change and how they can be cared for by different groups including First Nations Australians.

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students collect, sort and record information and data from observations and provided sources, including unscaled timelines and labelled maps or models.

standards.title: Technological change in everyday life

standards.title: Local First Nations interconnections

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students develop questions about objects, people, places and events in the past and present.

standards.title: Comparing places in the region

standards.description: the experiences of individuals and groups, including military and civilian officials, and convicts involved in the establishment of the first British colony
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the experiences of individuals and groups involved in the establishment of the first British colony.

standards.title: Effects of contact and invasion
standards.description: the effects of contact with other people on First Nations Australians and their Countries/Places following the arrival of the First Fleet and how this was viewed by First Nations Australians as an invasion

standards.description: the ways changing transportation and technologies are used to connect people to services, information and people in other places
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how changing transportation and technologies connect people to services, information and other places.

standards.title: Travel choices and place impacts
standards.description: the effects on places of people's travel, recreational, cultural or leisure choices, and the strategies for managing the impacts on these places
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the effects on places of travel and leisure choices and strategies for managing these impacts.

standards.title: Trade interconnections
standards.description: the ways that places and people are interconnected with other places through trade in goods and services, at all scales
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how places and people are interconnected through trade at different scales.

standards.title: Consumption and global sustainability
standards.description: the impacts of the production and consumption of goods on places throughout the world, and strategies to manage sustainability in these places
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the impacts of production and consumption on places and strategies to manage sustainability.

standards.title: Human-induced environmental change
standards.description: the human-induced changes that challenge the sustainability of places and environments
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the human-induced changes that challenge the sustainability of places and environments.

standards.title: Environmental worldviews
standards.description: the environmental world views of people and their implications for environmental management
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain environmental worldviews and their implications for environmental management.

standards.title: First Nations environmental management
standards.description: First Nations Australians' approaches to custodial responsibility and environmental management in different regions of Australia
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain First Nations Australians' approaches to custodial responsibility and environmental management.

standards.title: Managing environmental change
standards.description: causes and effects of a change in an identified environment at a local, national or global scale, and strategies to manage sustainability
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the causes and effects of environmental change at different scales and strategies to manage sustainability.

standards.title: Measuring human wellbeing
standards.description: the methods used to measure spatial variations in human wellbeing and development, and how these can be applied to determine differences between places at the global scale
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain methods used to measure spatial variations in human wellbeing and apply them to differences between places.

standards.title: Regional wellbeing variation
standards.description: reasons for, and consequences of, spatial variations in human wellbeing at a regional and national scale, drawing on studies such as from within India or another country in Asia
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain reasons for and consequences of spatial variations in human wellbeing at regional and national scales.

standards.title: Wellbeing variation in Australia
standards.description: reasons for, and consequences of, spatial variations in human wellbeing in Australia, including for First Nations Australians
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain reasons for and consequences of spatial variations in human wellbeing in Australia including for First Nations Australians.

standards.title: Responses to improve wellbeing
standards.description: responses of international and national government and non-government organisations to improve human wellbeing in Australia, within India and another country in the Pacific
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain responses of international and national organisations to improve human wellbeing in different places.

standards.title: Early human migration
standards.description: theories and historical interpretations about early human evolution and migration, such as the theory that people moved out of Africa and the causes of migration to other parts of the world, including Australia
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain theories about early human evolution and migration including movement to Australia.

standards.title: Arrival on the Australian continent
standards.description: theories about the causes and effects of the arrival of early First Nations Australians on the Australian continent and their migration routes across the continent
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain theories about the arrival of early First Nations Australians and their migration routes.

standards.title: Continuity over deep time
standards.description: how First Nations Australians are the world's oldest continuing cultures, displaying evidence of both continuity and change over deep time
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how First Nations Australians are the world's oldest continuing cultures showing continuity and change.

standards.title: Environmental response over time
standards.description: how First Nations Australians have responded to environmental processes and changes over time
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how First Nations Australians responded to environmental processes and changes over time.

standards.title: Early technological achievements
standards.description: the technological achievements of early First Nations Australians, and how these developed in different places and contributed to daily life, and land and water source management
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain technological achievements of early First Nations Australians and their contribution to daily life and land management.

standards.title: Social organisation and cultural practice
standards.description: the social organisation and cultural practices of early First Nations Australians, and their continuity and change over time
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the social organisation and cultural practices of early First Nations Australians and their continuity and change.

standards.title: Cultural preservation and heritage
standards.description: the cultural obligations of First Nations Australians about significant heritage sites, including ancestral remains, material culture and artefacts, and the role of collaboration between First Nations Australians and other individuals and groups to ensure cultural preservation
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain cultural obligations relating to heritage sites and the role of collaboration in cultural preservation.

standards.title: Historical and archaeological evidence
standards.description: the different methods and sources of evidence used by historians and archaeologists to investigate early societies, and the importance of archaeology and conserving the remains, material culture and heritage of the past
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain methods and sources used to investigate early societies and the importance of archaeology and conservation.

standards.title: Environment and ancient development
standards.description: how the physical environment and geographical features influenced the development of the ancient society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how physical environment influenced the development of an ancient society.

standards.title: Roles and groups in ancient society
standards.description: the organisation and roles of key groups in ancient society such as the nobility, bureaucracy, women and slaves, and how they influenced and changed society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the organisation and roles of key groups in ancient society and how they influenced change.

standards.title: Beliefs, values and practices
standards.description: key beliefs, values and practices of an ancient society, with a particular emphasis on one of the following areas: everyday life, warfare, or death and funerary customs
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain key beliefs, values and practices of an ancient society.

standards.title: Contacts, conflicts and change
standards.description: causes and effects of contacts and conflicts within ancient societies and/or with other societies, resulting in developments such as the conquest of other lands, the expansion of trade and peace treaties
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the causes and effects of contacts and conflicts within and between ancient societies.

standards.title: Significant individual in ancient society
standards.description: the role and achievements of a significant individual in an ancient society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the role and achievements of a significant individual in an ancient society.

standards.title: Transformation to early modern world
standards.description: the transformation of the ancient world to the early modern world, from the decline of the Roman Empire in western Europe through Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the transformation from the ancient world to the early modern world.

standards.title: Groups in Medieval Europe
standards.description: the roles and relationships of different groups in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the roles and relationships of different groups in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe.

standards.title: Turning points in Medieval Europe
standards.description: a significant event, development, turning point or challenge that contributed to continuity and change in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain a significant turning point that contributed to continuity and change in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe.

standards.title: Power and authority in Medieval Europe
standards.description: the experiences and perspectives of rulers and of subject peoples, and the interaction between power and/or authority in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain experiences and perspectives of rulers and subjects, and the interaction between power and authority in Medieval Europe.

standards.title: Significant individuals in Medieval Europe
standards.description: the role and achievements of a significant individual and/or group in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the role and achievements of a significant individual or group in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe.

standards.title: Interpretations of Medieval Europe
standards.description: interpretations about an event, individual, group, institution or movement in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain interpretations about an event, individual, group, institution or movement in Medieval, Renaissance or pre-modern Europe.

standards.title: Features of empire and expansion
standards.description: the significant social, religious, cultural, economic, environmental and/or political features of different groups related to the empire and/or expansion
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain significant features of groups related to empire and expansion.

standards.title: Turning points in empire
standards.description: a significant event, development, turning point or challenge that contributed to continuity and change related to the empire and/or expansion
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain a significant turning point related to empire and expansion.

standards.title: Power and authority in empire
standards.description: the experiences and perspectives of rulers and of subject peoples, and how the interaction between power and/or authority relates to the empire and/or expansion
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain experiences and perspectives of rulers and subjects and the interaction between power and authority in empire.

standards.title: Significant individuals in empire
standards.description: the role and achievements of a significant individual and/or group connected to the empire and/or expansion
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the role and achievements of a significant individual or group connected to empire and expansion.

standards.title: Interpretations of empire
standards.description: interpretations about the society and events, and/or individuals and/or groups connected to the empire and/or expansion
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain interpretations about societies, events, individuals and groups connected to empire and expansion.

standards.title: Features of an Asia-Pacific society
standards.description: the significant social, religious, cultural, economic, environmental and/or political features of different groups in the Asian-Pacific society

standards.title: Turning points in the Asia-Pacific world
standards.description: a significant development, event, turning point or challenge that contributed to continuity and change in the Asian-Pacific society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain a significant turning point that contributed to continuity and change in an Asia-Pacific society.

standards.title: Power and authority in Asia-Pacific
standards.description: the experiences and perspectives of rulers and of subject peoples, and the interaction between power and/or authority in the Asian-Pacific society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain experiences and perspectives of rulers and subjects and the interaction between power and authority in an Asia-Pacific society.

standards.title: Significant individuals in Asia-Pacific
standards.description: the role and achievements of a significant individual and/or group in the Asian-Pacific society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the role and achievements of a significant individual or group in an Asia-Pacific society.

standards.title: Interpretations of Asia-Pacific world
standards.description: interpretations about the Asian-Pacific society and events, and/or individuals and/or groups connected to the society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain interpretations about an Asia-Pacific society and related events, individuals and groups.

standards.title: European imperial expansion

standards.title: Changes in Australian society
standards.description: the key social, cultural, economic and political changes and their significance in the development of Australian society during the period

standards.title: Contact and First Nations impact
standards.description: the causes and effects of European contact and extension of settlement, including their impact on the First Nations Peoples of Australia
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the causes and effects of European contact and settlement including impacts on First Nations Peoples.

standards.title: Events and movements in Australian development
standards.description: significant events, ideas, people, groups and movements in the development of Australian society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain significant events, ideas, people, groups and movements in the development of Australian society.

standards.title: Continuity and change in Australian life
standards.description: continuities and changes and their effects on ways of life and living conditions, political and legal institutions, and cultural expression around the turn of the 20th century in Australian society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain continuities and changes and their effects on ways of life, institutions and cultural expression in Australian society.

standards.title: Perspectives on colonisation
standards.description: different experiences and perspectives of colonisers, settlers and First Nations Australians and the impact of these experiences on changes to Australian society's ideas, beliefs and values
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain different perspectives of colonisers, settlers and First Nations Australians and their impact on Australian society.

standards.title: Australia in a changing world
standards.description: the development of Australian society in relation to other nations in the world by 1914, including the effects of ideas and movements of people
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the development of Australian society in relation to other nations by 1914.

standards.title: Causes of the First World War
standards.description: the causes of the First World War and the reasons why Australians enlisted to fight in the war

standards.title: Australian experiences of war

standards.title: Turning points of the First World War
standards.description: significant events and turning points of the war and the nature of warfare, including the Western Front Battle of the Somme and the Armistice
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain significant events and turning points of the First World War and the nature of warfare.

standards.title: Effects of the First World War
standards.description: the effects of the First World War on Australian society, such as the role of women, political debates about conscription, relationships with the British Empire, and the experiences of returned soldiers
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the effects of the First World War on Australian society.

standards.title: Commemoration and Anzac interpretations
standards.description: the commemoration of the First World War, including different historical interpretations and debates about the nature and significance of the Anzac legend and the war
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the commemoration of the First World War including interpretations and debates about the Anzac legend.

standards.title: Industrial Revolution causes and effects
standards.description: the social, economic, political, technological and/or environmental causes and effects of the Industrial Revolution on Europe in the late 18th and 19th century
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the causes and effects of the Industrial Revolution on Europe.

standards.title: Population movement and settlement
standards.description: the changing population movements and settlement patterns during the period 1750 to 1900

standards.title: Effects of population movement
standards.description: the short-, medium- and long-term effects of population movements and changing settlement patterns during this period, such as global demographic changes, transport, new ideas, and political and social reforms

standards.title: Experiences during the Industrial Revolution
standards.description: the different perspectives and experiences of men, women and children during the Industrial Revolution, and their changing way of life
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the perspectives and experiences of men, women and children during the Industrial Revolution.

standards.title: Ideas shaping modern society
standards.description: the ideas that emerged and influenced change in society, such as nationalism, capitalism, imperialism, socialism, egalitarianism and Chartism

standards.title: Groups promoting change

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the role of a significant individual or group in promoting ideas during the Industrial Revolution.

standards.title: Features of an Asian society

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain key features of an Asian society during the 18th and early 19th century.

standards.title: European contact in Asia
standards.description: the causes and effects of European contact, including colonialisation, on an Asian society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the causes and effects of European contact including colonisation on an Asian society.

standards.title: Developments in an Asian society
standards.description: significant events, ideas, people, groups and/or movements in the development of an Asian society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain significant events, ideas, people, groups and movements in the development of an Asian society.

standards.title: Continuity and change in an Asian society
standards.description: continuities and changes and their effects on the ways of life and living conditions, political and legal institutions, and cultural expression around the turn of the 20th century in an Asian society
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain continuities and changes and their effects on ways of life in an Asian society.

standards.title: Perspectives on colonisation in Asia
standards.description: different experiences and perspectives of colonisers and Asian peoples from the time and the impact of changes to society, including events, ideas, beliefs and values
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain different perspectives of colonisers and Asian peoples and the impact of changes to society.

standards.title: Asia in a changing world
standards.description: the development of an Asian society in relation to other nations in the world by 1914, including the effects of ideas such as nationalism and self-determination
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the development of an Asian society in relation to other nations by 1914.

standards.title: Causes of the Second World War
standards.description: the causes, outbreak and course of the Second World War and the significance of Australian involvement
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the causes, outbreak and course of the Second World War and the significance of Australian involvement.

standards.title: Australian experiences in WW2
standards.description: the places where Australians fought, and their perspectives and experiences during the Second World War, such as the fall of Singapore, prisoners of war (POWs), the Battle of Britain and Kokoda
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain where Australians fought and their perspectives and experiences during the Second World War.

standards.title: Turning points of the Second World War
standards.description: the significant events and turning points of the Second World War, including the Holocaust and use of the atomic bomb
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain significant events and turning points of the Second World War including the Holocaust and atomic bomb.

standards.title: Home front continuity and change

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the effects of the Second World War with emphasis on continuity and change on the Australian home front.

standards.title: Post-war significance for Australia
standards.description: the significance of the Second World War to Australia's immediate post-war economic, political and social development, and Australia's international relationships in the 20th century
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the significance of the Second World War to Australia's post-war development and international relationships.

standards.title: Commemoration and debate

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the commemoration of the Second World War including interpretations and debates.

standards.title: Post-war global influences

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the effects of significant post-war world events, ideas and developments on Australian society.

standards.title: Changing perspectives on migration

standards.title: First Nations rights campaigns

standards.title: Contributions to First Nations rights

standards.title: Civil rights events and methods

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain significant events and methods in the civil rights movement for First Nations Australians.

standards.title: Women's movement
standards.description: the significant events, individuals and groups in the women's movement in Australia, and how they have changed the role and status of women
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain significant events, individuals and groups in the women's movement and how they changed the role and status of women.

standards.title: Continuing struggles for rights
standards.description: the continuing efforts to create change in the civil rights and freedoms in Australia, for First Nations Australians, migrants and women

standards.title: Changing perspectives on modern life

standards.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights

standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain causes and effects of major global influences on Australia in the post-war period.

standards.title: Changing conditions in post-war Australia
standards.description: changing social, political, economic, cultural, environmental and technological conditions, and the causes of a major global influence in Australia
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain changing conditions and causes of a major global influence in Australia.

standards.title: Continuity and change in Australian life
standards.description: continuities and changes in perspectives, responses, beliefs and values that have influenced the Australian way of life
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain continuities and changes in perspectives and values that have influenced the Australian way of life.

standards.title: Global influences on national identity
standards.description: the effects of global influences on Australia's changing identity as a nation and its international relationships
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain the effects of global influences on Australia's changing national identity and international relationships.

standards.title: Historical debates
